mainTopic: The proofs about קריאת הגבר, then the ten miracles of the בית המקדש and how the גמרא arrives at exactly ten.
overview: This amud first finishes the argument over what קריאת הגבר means. רב says it is the Temple crier's call, and רבי שילא says it is the rooster's crow. The end of a ברייתא about voices heard across the world supports רב. A ברייתא about the danger of traveling at night before the rooster crows supports רבי שילא. Next, רב יהודה quotes רב: on the רגלים the people stood packed together, yet they bowed with room to spare. The גמרא explains that this was one of the ten miracles of the מקדש and quotes the משנה that lists them. It then works through the count. Some items happened in ירושלים, other Temple miracles are added, similar miracles are grouped, and miracles hidden from the public are left out. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to prove, from ריש לקיש's teaching about the 'pure table,' that the warm לחם הפנים was a miracle the public could see. That proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא supporting רב: רידיא and the soul's voice
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about sounds heard across the world ends: some add the voice of רידיא, and the גמרא then adds that the רבנן prayed that the soul's cry when it leaves the body be canceled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: the voice of רידיא is also heard from one end of the world to the other. And the Sages prayed for mercy about the voice of the soul as it leaves the body, and they had it canceled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began earlier. That ברייתא lists loud sounds, and it treats קריאת הגבר as a human crier's call, which supports רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists sounds so loud they travel across the world. The יש אומרים adds רידיא, the מלאך in charge of rain and watering the earth. The גמרא's own added note (in Aramaic) about the soul shows that the רבנן prayed for this painful sound to stop being heard. Because the list is about human and heavenly voices, it fits רב's reading that גבר means a man, the Temple crier.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: an alternate opinion inside the ברייתא
רידיא, the מלאך appointed over rain and watering the earth
They asked for mercy (they prayed)
The soul
They canceled it (had it nullified)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement. It is the end of a ברייתא the גמרא started quoting on the previous amud, and it serves as a proof for רב's view of קריאת הגבר.

phrases.english: And some say: Ridya as well.
phrases.notes: רידיא is the angel over rain, whose voice calls to the heavens and the deep.

phrases.english: And the Sages asked for mercy regarding the soul
at the moment that it leaves the body,
and they had it canceled.
phrases.notes: Its sound is no longer heard across the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא that began on the previous amud, which serves as support for רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that קריאת הגבר means the call of the Temple crier.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא listing voices heard from one end of the world to the other.

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting רבי שילא: traveling before the rooster crows
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that someone who travels before קריאת הגבר is responsible for whatever harm comes to him. This supports רבי שילא's view that גבר means the rooster.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that supports רבי שילא: Someone who sets out on the road before קריאת הגבר, his blood is on his own head.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא brings a proof for the other side. Here קריאת הגבר clearly means a rooster's crow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Traveling at night before the rooster crows was considered dangerous, because of מזיקין (harmful spirits). If the person is hurt, it is his own fault. In this case 'the call of the גבר' plainly means the rooster crowing at dawn, so it supports רבי שילא.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that supports him
One who sets out on a journey
The 'call of the gever,' meaning a crier or a rooster depending on the view
His blood is on his own head; he is to blame for his own harm

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the phrase קריאת הגבר is used in both senses in different sources. That is why both רב and רבי שילא can find support.

phrases.english: A baraita was taught in accordance with Rabbi Sheila:
One who sets out on the road before the rooster's call —
his blood is on his own head.
phrases.notes: He is at fault if harmed, for example by מזיקין at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for רב, the גמרא brings a parallel proof for רבי שילא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שילא's view that קריאת הגבר means the rooster's crow.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the danger of traveling at night before the rooster crows.

steps.title: How many crows: twice or three times
steps.stepSummary: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי יאשיה says one must wait until the rooster crows twice. The יש אומרים say three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה says: one must wait until it crows a second time. And some say: until it crows a third time.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It adds a disagreement about how many times the rooster must crow before it is safe to travel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion seems to allow travel after a single crow. רבי יאשיה requires two crows, and the יש אומרים require three. Counting crows only makes sense for a rooster, so this strengthens the proof for רבי שילא.

keyTerms.meaning: Until it does it a second time (crows twice)
Until it does it a third time (crows three times)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya says: until it crows a second time,
and some say: until it crows a third time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and refines how long one must wait.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יאשיה: wait for two crows. יש אומרים: wait for three crows.

steps.title: Which rooster counts: a medium one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks which kind of rooster sets the time. The answer is an ordinary, medium rooster.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about which rooster did they say this? About a medium rooster.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by clarifying which rooster is the standard. It asks the question and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roosters do not all crow at the same time; some crow early and some late. So the ברייתא sets a typical, medium rooster as the measure. This detail again shows the ברייתא is talking about a real rooster, which supports רבי שילא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rooster
Medium, average, typical
In which one? About which?

steps.whatToRemember: There are two proofs. The ברייתא of the loud voices supports רב (קריאת הגבר is a human crier). The ברייתא about traveling at night supports רבי שילא (קריאת הגבר is a rooster).

phrases.english: And about which rooster did they say this? —
about a medium rooster.
phrases.notes: Neither one that crows unusually early nor one that crows unusually late.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the standard used in the rule from the previous steps.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which rooster's crowing sets the time?

steps.title: רב: on the Festivals they stood crowded but bowed with space
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב. When ישראל came up for the רגל, they stood squeezed together, yet when they bowed there was room. The crowd stretched eleven אמות behind the בית הכפורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: When ישראל go up for the Festival, they stand crowded but bow with space between them. And they extend eleven אמות behind the בית הכפורת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. It quotes רב's description of the crowd in the עזרה during the רגלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing, people were packed tightly. When they bowed down and confessed, each person had room, so no one heard another's ווידוי. The crowd was so large that people even filled the eleven-אמה strip behind the קודש הקדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Going up to Jerusalem for a pilgrimage Festival
Crowded, packed tightly
With space, spread out
Bowing down (prostrating)
The Hall of the Ark Cover, meaning the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
When the Jewish people go up for the Festival,
they stand crowded but bow with space,
and they extend eleven cubits
behind the Hall of the Ark Cover.
phrases.notes: The area behind the קודש הקדשים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, unrelated to the proofs about קריאת הגבר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the רגל the people stood packed but bowed with room, and the crowd extended eleven אמות behind the בית הכפורת.

steps.title: What is רב saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב means, especially with the detail about eleven אמות behind the בית הכפורת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask what רב's statement means. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's statement reads like a list of separate facts, and their connection is unclear. In particular, why mention the eleven אמות? The גמרא wants to know the point he is making.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? (asking what a statement means)

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the point of רב's statement, and how do its parts fit together?

steps.title: רב is describing a miracle
steps.stepSummary: Even though the crowd was so huge that it filled eleven אמות behind the בית הכפורת and people stood packed, they bowed with room. This was one of the ten miracles in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: Even though they extended eleven אמות behind the בית הכפורת and stood crowded, when they bowed, they bowed with space. And this is one of the ten miracles that happened in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב's words describe a single miracle. The size of the crowd is mentioned to show how impossible the extra space was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eleven אמות detail proves how full the place was. With people packed even behind the קודש הקדשים, there should have been no room to bow. Yet everyone had space, so it was a נס, and it fits into the list of ten miracles.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is saying (introducing an explanation)
Even though
Miracles

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּמְשָׁכִין אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה
phrases.english: Even though they extend eleven cubits
behind the Hall of the Ark Cover, and stand crowded,
when they bow — they bow with space,
and this is one of the ten miracles
that were performed in the Temple.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The eleven אמות detail shows how packed the place was. The room to bow despite this was a miracle, one of the ten miracles of the מקדש.

steps.title: The משנה of the ten miracles in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the claim with the משנה listing the miracles of the בית המקדש, which includes 'standing crowded and bowing with space.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Ten miracles were done in the בית המקדש. No woman miscarried from the smell of the sacrificial meat. The sacrificial meat never rotted. No fly was seen in the slaughterhouse. The כהן גדול never had a seminal emission on יום כיפור. No disqualification was found in the עומר, the שתי הלחם, or the לחם הפנים. They stood crowded and bowed with space. No snake or scorpion ever harmed anyone in Jerusalem. And no one ever said to his friend, 'There is no room for me to stay overnight in Jerusalem.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה to prove that 'standing crowded, bowing with space' is listed as one of the Temple's miracles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item describes something that naturally should have happened but never did. Examples are meat rotting, flies near blood, or a disqualification in an offering that could not be replaced. The item 'עומדים צפופים ומשתחוים רווחים' appears right in the list, which confirms רב's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Sacrificial meat
A seminal emission, which would make the כהן גדול טמא
The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
The showbread placed on the שולחן every שבת

steps.confusionAlert: The list really does reach ten, because the three 'no disqualification' items (עומר, שתי הלחם, לחם הפנים) are counted separately. The גמרא says so in step 12: פסולי תלתא הוו. The real problem, raised in step 9, is that two of the ten items happened in ירושלים, not in the מקדש. The parallel list in פרקי אבות is different and includes the rain and smoke miracles that the גמרא brings in step 10.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's teaching about standing packed but bowing with room is not just a description. It is one of the ten famous miracles of the בית המקדש, as the משנה states.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן, עֲשָׂרָה נִסִּים נַעֲשׂוּ בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ:
phrases.english: As we learned: Ten miracles were performed in the Temple:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִפִּילָה אִשָּׁה מֵרֵיחַ בְּשַׂר הַקֹּדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: No woman miscarried from the aroma of the sacrificial meat.
phrases.notes: A pregnant woman's unmet craving could cause a miscarriage.

phrases.english: And the sacrificial meat never rotted.
And no fly was seen in the slaughterhouse.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֵירַע קֶרִי לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: And the High Priest never had a seminal emission on Yom Kippur.
And no disqualification was found in the omer,
or in the two loaves, or in the showbread.
phrases.notes: These could not easily be replaced if disqualified.

phrases.english: They stand crowded, yet bow with space.
phrases.notes: This is the item that supports רב.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הִזִּיק נָחָשׁ וְעַקְרָב בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם מֵעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: And neither snake nor scorpion ever caused harm in Jerusalem.
And no person ever said to his friend:
The place is too cramped for me to stay overnight in Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, עֲשָׂרָה נִסִּים נַעֲשׂוּ בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in step 7 that this was one of the ten miracles.
steps.raayaObject: That standing crowded but bowing with space was one of the ten miracles of the מקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (a parallel but somewhat different list appears in פרקי אבות) listing the ten miracles in the בית המקדש.

steps.title: The list starts in the Temple but ends in Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה's list of ten Temple miracles closes with miracles that happened in ירושלים, so there are not really ten in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The list opened with the Temple and ended with Jerusalem!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that there were ten miracles in the מקדש, because the last items on the list happened in ירושלים, not in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is called 'ten miracles in the מקדש.' But its final items, such as no one being hurt in ירושלים, are about the city. That leaves fewer than ten miracles that actually happened in the מקדש itself.

keyTerms.meaning: He opened, began
He ended, closed
The Holy Temple
Jerusalem, the city around the Temple

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not doubting that these events were miracles. It only questions whether they belong in a count of miracles that happened inside the מקדש.

phrases.english: He opened with the Temple,
and closed with Jerusalem!
phrases.notes: The last items on the list are miracles in the city, not in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source that was just quoted as proof in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The count of 'ten miracles in the מקדש'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some items on the list happened in ירושלים, so the count of miracles inside the מקדש falls below ten.

steps.title: Two more Temple miracles: rain and smoke
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there are two other Temple miracles: rain never put out the altar fire, and wind never moved its smoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two other miracles in the Temple. As a ברייתא teaches: rain never put out the fire on the altar's wood pile. And the smoke of the altar fire went straight up; even if every wind in the world blew on it, it would not move from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills the gap with two other miracles that clearly happened in the מקדש, using a ברייתא as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ירושלים miracles are taken off the Temple count and replaced with two altar miracles. The altar stood in an open courtyard, so it was exposed to rain and wind. Its fire and smoke staying unaffected were miracles that happened inside the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Two other ones
The wood pile arranged on the altar
The smoke rising from the altar fire
Move, shift

phrases.english: There are two other miracles in the Temple.
As it was taught: rain never extinguished
the fire of the altar's wood pile.
phrases.notes: The altar was outside, open to the sky.

phrases.english: And the smoke of the altar pile,
even if all the winds in the world
come and blow on it,
they do not move it from its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9 by swapping in two Temple miracles.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Substitution: replacing the ירושלים miracles with other Temple miracles
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Temple list is short by two miracles.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rain and smoke miracles complete the count of ten.

steps.title: Even more Temple miracles: things swallowed into the ground
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether there are no other miracles. It quotes more of them, which would push the count above ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are there no more? But רב שמעיה taught in קלנבו: broken clay pots were swallowed up in their place. And אביי said: the crop and feathers of bird offerings, the ashes of the inner altar, and the ashes of the מנורה were swallowed up in their place!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the problem flips. The גמרא brings more Temple miracles, so the count is too high instead of too low.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clay pots used for holy meat had to be broken, and their pieces disappeared into the floor. In the same way, אביי says that certain leftovers like bird crops, feathers, and ashes disappeared where they were placed. Adding these miracles goes beyond ten.

keyTerms.meaning: And are there no more?
Broken pieces of clay vessels
Swallowed up in their place
The crop and feathers of a bird offering
Removal of ashes

phrases.english: And are there no more?
But didn't Rav Shemaya teach in Kalnevo:
phrases.notes: קלנבו is the name of a place.

phrases.english: shards of clay vessels were swallowed up in their place,
and Abaye said: the crop and the feathers,
and the ashes of the inner altar,
and the ashes of the candelabrum,
were swallowed up in their place!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ לֵיכָּא? וְהָתַנְיָא רַב שְׁמַעְיָה בְּקַלְנְבוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new total reached in Step 10 by showing there are extra miracles.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Additional known Temple miracles make the total more than ten.

steps.title: Count the three 'no disqualification' miracles as one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא groups the three similar miracles about no disqualification being found into one. This frees two spots for the swallowing miracles.
steps.simpleTranslation: The disqualification miracles were three? Count them as one. Take out two, and bring in two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the overcount by treating three similar miracles as a single miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No disqualification was ever found in the עומר, the שתי הלחם, or the לחם הפנים. These were counted as three miracles, but they are really one type. Counting them as one opens two places on the list for the two swallowing miracles.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualifications (no disqualification was ever found)
Count them as one
Take out
Bring in

phrases.english: The disqualification miracles were three?
phrases.notes: These are the עומר, the שתי הלחם, and the לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: Count them as one,
remove two and bring in two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the overcount raised in Step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each disqualification miracle counts on its own, so the list goes over ten.
steps.terutzMaskana: Similar miracles count as one, so the swallowing miracles fit within ten.

steps.title: By that logic, the swallowing miracles should also count as one
steps.stepSummary: If similar miracles are grouped, then the two swallowing miracles must also be grouped as one, and now the list is one short.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the swallowing miracles are also two? Count them as one. Then the list is missing one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the grouping rule against itself. Using the same rule leaves the list with only nine miracles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shards and אביי's items are both 'swallowed in place,' so they are one type of miracle. Grouping them gives one miracle instead of two, which leaves the count at nine.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
The swallowed items
They are missing one

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, בְּלוּעִין נָמֵי תְּרֵי הָווּ?
phrases.english: If so, the swallowed ones are also two?
Count them as one.
Then they are lacking one!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בְּלוּעִין נָמֵי תְּרֵי הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies Step 12's grouping rule consistently, which causes a new shortage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applying the grouping rule consistently leaves only nine miracles.

steps.title: The warm לחם הפנים completes the ten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another Temple miracle from רבי יהושע בן לוי: the לחם הפנים was as warm when it was removed as when it was set out.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is another one. As רבי יהושע בן לוי said: a great miracle happened with the לחם הפנים. When it was removed, it was just like when it was set out, as the verse says: 'to put out warm bread on the day it was taken away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills the missing spot with one more Temple miracle, backed by a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לחם הפנים sat on the שלחן for a whole week, yet it stayed fresh and warm. The verse calls it 'warm bread' on the day it was taken away, which proves the miracle. This brings the count back to ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Another one
The showbread placed weekly on the Temple table
Its removal was like its setting out (just as fresh and warm)
Warm bread

phrases.english: There is also another one,
as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: נֵס גָּדוֹל הָיָה נַעֲשָׂה בְּלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים,
phrases.english: a great miracle was done with the showbread,
its removal was like its arrangement,
phrases.notes: After a full week, it was still warm and fresh.

phrases.english: as it says: 'to put out warm bread on the day it was taken away.'
phrases.notes: The verse is from שמואל א כא:ז.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא נָמֵי אַחֲרִיתִי, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills the shortage created in Step 13.
steps.terutzMaskana: The warm לחם הפנים is the tenth miracle.
steps.whatToRemember: The count now stands at ten: similar miracles are grouped as one, and the warm לחם הפנים fills the last spot.

steps.title: More miracles: the ארון and the כרובים took up no space
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again whether there are no more miracles, quoting רבי לוי about the ארון and שמואל about the כרובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are there no more? But רבי לוי said: we have this tradition from our fathers, that the place of the ארון was not part of the measurement. And רבנאי said in the name of שמואל: the כרובים stood by a miracle!
steps.whatsHappening: The count reached ten, and now the גמרא challenges it again with two more Temple miracles. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קודש הקדשים was twenty אמות wide, and there were ten אמות of space on each side of the ארון. That means the ארון took up no space at all. The כרובים' wings spanned the full twenty אמות, so their bodies had no room either. These are two more miracles, which again push the count past ten.

keyTerms.meaning: A tradition we hold
The space taken up by the Ark
Is not part of the measurement (it took up no space)
The golden winged figures in the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: And are there no more?
But didn't Rabbi Levi say:
this matter is a tradition in our hands from our fathers:
the place of the Ark is not part of the measurement.
phrases.notes: The ארון took up no physical space in the room.

phrases.english: And Rabbenai said in the name of Shmuel:
the cherubs stood by a miracle!
phrases.notes: Their wings filled the whole width, leaving no room for their bodies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ten-miracle total reached in Step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two more miracles inside the מקדש, the ארון and the כרובים, push the total above ten.

steps.title: Only miracles the public could see are counted
steps.stepSummary: The list counts outside, public miracles. It does not count inside, hidden ones like those of the ארון and the כרובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא counts miracles that happened outside, where everyone could see them. He does not count miracles that happened inside, where people could not see them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15 about why the miracles of the ארון and the כרובים are missing from the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארון and the כרובים stood in the קודש הקדשים, where nobody went except the כהן גדול once a year. So their miracles were hidden from the people. The list of ten only includes miracles that the crowds could actually witness.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside miracles, the ones the public could see
Inside miracles, the ones hidden from the public
He counts (he lists it)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that decides what makes it onto the list. Every miracle from now on will be checked against it.

phrases.english: Outside miracles, he counts;
phrases.notes: דְבָרַאי comes from בָּרָא, meaning outside.

phrases.english: inside miracles, he does not count.
phrases.notes: דְגַוַּאי comes from גַּו, meaning inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the miracles of the ארון and the כרובים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Sets a limiting rule for which miracles count (public versus hidden)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any miracle in the מקדש should be on the list, so the ארון and כרובים miracles are missing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only miracles visible to the public are listed, so the hidden miracles of the ארון and the כרובים are rightly left out.

steps.title: But the לחם הפנים was also inside
steps.stepSummary: If inside miracles are not counted, why is the לחם הפנים on the list? The שולחן stood inside the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the לחם הפנים is also an inside miracle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule it just made by pointing to a miracle that is on the list even though it happened inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שולחן holding the לחם הפנים was inside the היכל, where ordinary people could not go. In step 14, the miracle of the bread staying warm was added to the list. That seems to break the "outside only" rule.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your rule is true)
The showbread placed on the שולחן in the היכל

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים נָמֵי נִיסֵּי דְגַוַּאי הוּא!
phrases.english: the showbread too is an inside miracle!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים נָמֵי נִיסֵּי דְגַוַּאי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from step 16 using the miracle added in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only outside miracles are counted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The לחם הפנים was inside the היכל, yet it was counted. So either the rule is wrong or the לחם הפנים does not belong on the list.

steps.title: The לחם הפנים miracle was seen by the public
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the לחם הפנים counts as an outside miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: The לחם הפנים is an outside miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps its rule and claims that the לחם הפנים miracle really was visible to the public. It is setting up a source to prove this in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule stays the same. What changes is how the לחם הפנים is classified: even though the bread usually sat inside, people did get to see the miracle. The proof of how they saw it comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is

phrases.english: The showbread is an outside miracle,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by reclassifying the לחם הפנים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassification: the case is placed in the other category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The לחם הפנים was a hidden inside miracle.
steps.terutzMaskana: The לחם הפנים miracle was seen by the public, so it fits the rule.

steps.title: ריש לקיש on the pure table
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads the words "the pure table" to mean that the שולחן could become impure. This is the start of the proof that the bread was shown publicly.
steps.simpleTranslation: As ריש לקיש said: What does the פסוק mean when it says "on the pure table"? Calling it "pure" teaches that it is the kind of thing that can become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings ריש לקיש to back up the claim that the לחם הפנים miracle was public. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a wooden object fixed in place cannot become טמא, so why would the תורה need to stress that the שולחן is "pure"? ריש לקיש learns that the שולחן could become טמא, which means it was treated as a movable vessel. The גמרא will go on to show how this connects to the people seeing the warm bread.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
What is the meaning of what is written
The pure table that held the לחם הפנים
By implication (you can learn from this)
Ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not yet explain how the people saw the bread. It only establishes that the שולחן could become טמא. The connection to the public comes in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: as Reish Lakish said:
What is that which is written,
"on the pure table"?
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in ויקרא כד:ו.

phrases.english: "Pure" implies that it can be impure,

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מַאי דִּכְתִיב עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן הַטָּהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the claim in step 18
steps.raayaObject: That the לחם הפנים miracle was visible to the public
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's reading of "עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן הַטָּהוֹר" (ויקרא כד:ו), which shows the שולחן could become טמא
